presets.name: G1 · Writing — draft from raw material

custom.task.statement: The message must accomplish: {{what the reader should know / decide / do}}.

custom.context.rationale: Profile the data first (rows, columns, date range, nulls, duplicate keys) and show me the profile BEFORE analyzing. Reconcile to the known total: {{anchor number and its source}}.

custom.format.structure: Table: criterion | score | 1–2 verbatim quotes as evidence | what a 5 would have contained. Then: the 3 biggest gaps, and the 3 questions I should ask the author.

custom.task.statement:
A colleague's draft/plan is below. Do not say whether you agree, and do not compliment it.
1. Steelman the OPPOSITE position — the strongest honest case against.
2. The 3 weakest points, each with why it fails and how a critic would attack it.
3. What evidence, if it existed, would prove this wrong? What should be checked first?
4. Only after all that: your overall read, hedges included.

Build an .xlsx workbook: {{one line — what it is for and who reads it}}.
Tabs: README (purpose, sources with as-of date, every metric defined, assumptions, change log) · Data (clean rows, one row = {{grain}}, one header row, no merged cells, codes as text) · Summary ({{the pivot/aggregate view}}).
Formulas, not pasted values, wherever a number derives from the data.
custom.format.structure: Before finishing: verify totals on Summary reconcile to Data row counts, and show me the check.

custom.task.statement: Turn the material below into {{n}} slides max. Every slide title states the takeaway in ≤ 12 words WITH the number ("Scrap fell 40% after the fixture change", never "Scrap update").

Build a SINGLE-FILE interactive HTML {{dashboard | calculator | tracker}} for {{audience}}: {{one line — the question it answers}}.
Views: {{KPI tiles: metric, value, vs target}} · {{main chart: type, x, y, filterable by …}} · {{sortable/searchable table}}.
custom.format.output_type: Format: one self-contained .html file — data embedded, works offline from disk, no external calls, no login.
custom.format.structure: Every number computed from the embedded data — nothing hard-coded I can't trace. Formulas shown on screen where users would want to audit them. Footer: as-of date + owner. Handle blank/zero inputs gracefully.
custom.context.rationale: This will be shared on locked-down laptops — self-containment is a hard requirement, not styling.

custom.format.structure: 1. Answer in 3 sentences (say what's known vs contested). 2. Key findings — every bullet ends with its source link AND publication date; no link → label "unsourced — verify". 3. What the sources do NOT establish. 4. Confidence: high/med/low and what would raise it.
custom.the_stop.boundaries:
1. {{the research question}}
2. {{one follow-up if the answer is contested}}

custom.format.musts: End with: "What these documents do NOT cover that the reader will assume they do." For contractual/regulatory/numeric text: verbatim quotes with location, both versions — no paraphrase.
custom.task.statement: If comparing versions: substantive differences only (section | A says | B says | why it matters); do not assume newer = correct; flag regressions too.

custom.a_mission.goal: {{the question to answer, or the thing to produce — one sentence}}
custom.a_mission.decision: {{what someone will do differently depending on the answer}}
custom.a_mission.audience_deadline: {{who sees it, minutes they'll give it}} · due {{date}}
custom.a_inputs.register: S1 — {{name}} · {{path}} · {{format}} · one row = {{grain}} · owner {{who}} · known issues: {{…}}
custom.a_checks.anchor: {{a number you already trust, from outside this run}}
custom.a_process.phases: Phase 0 intake (restate + assumptions) → Phase 1 {{…}} → Phase 2 {{…}} → final QA

presets.name: A2 · ETL → Presentation — data to defensible slide

custom.a_mission.goal: {{e.g., "What is first-pass yield by site and part for {{period}}, and which site/defect mode is the gap?"}}
custom.a_mission.decision: {{where to focus resources next {{quarter}}, and whether {{target}} is credible}}
custom.a_mission.done: {{n}} slides in {{template}} + updated master workbook + CSV snapshot
custom.a_context.glossary: {{METRIC}} = {{numerator}} ÷ {{denominator}} at {{grain}}; zero denominator → NULL, excluded from averages.
custom.a_checks.anchor: {{Σ inspected = {{n}} per the current master / prior cycle headline}}
custom.a_plan.steps:
1. Extract: read-only, hash + profile every input, parse with explicit types, fix nothing
2. Transform: one schema, ordered rules each logged with row counts, layers L1 (rows) → L2 (grouped) → L3 (summary)
3. Validate: run every check, write the reconciliation table → GATE 2
4. Analyze: the numbered questions, in order, then stop
5. Present: headline titles with the number; n on every proportion → GATE 3 before rendering
custom.a_outputs.deliverables:
1. deliverables/{{DECK}}_MMDDYY.pptx ({{n}} slides + notes)
2. deliverables/{{MASTER}}_MMDDYY.xlsx (README, L1, L2, L3, Validation tabs)
3. deliverables/{{SNAPSHOT}}_MMDDYY.csv (L2 for BI)

presets.name: A3 · Recurring cycle — reuse by diff

custom.a_mission.goal: Run the {{job name}} cycle per the standing brief at {{path/to/brief.md}}. Everything in the brief holds unless changed below.
custom.a_inputs.register: This cycle only: {{new files at path, covering dates}} · unchanged: {{S2, R1}} · as-of date for outputs: {{MMDDYY}}
custom.a_checks.anchor: {{last cycle's headline numbers, from path/to/last deliverable}}
custom.a_process.phases: Start with Phase 0: restate what changed vs. last cycle as you understand it — so drift gets caught before data is touched.

presets.name: A4 · Workspace standing rules (CLAUDE.md)

custom.a_context.domain: {{Two sentences: the initiative, who runs it, what "good" means.}} Owner: {{name}} · Status log: CHANGES.md
custom.a_context.quirks: {{quirk → rule — the tribal knowledge that bites}}
custom.a_environment.confidentiality: {{what may leave this workspace, and in what form}}

presets.note: Paste the assembled block into the workspace's CLAUDE.md — it becomes standing memory every session inherits. Keep it ≤ 60 lines.

custom.a_mission.goal: Turn the {{~N}} documents in {{folder}} into {{tracker}}.xlsx — one row per document, so {{audience}} can {{see status at a glance}}.
custom.a_inputs.register:
Documents look like: {{one line}}. Known variants: {{older layout B without field X}}. Extraction schema — column | from where in the doc | format | if missing:
{{field}} | {{location}} | {{type}} | MISSING
custom.a_checks.anchor: row count = file count — every document produces exactly one row, even unreadable ones (flag UNREADABLE)
custom.a_checks.hard: a value not stated verbatim = MISSING; uncertain reading = best reading + VERIFY flag — never a silent guess
custom.a_checks.soft: any field > {{20}}% MISSING — probably a layout variant; show me 2 example files
custom.a_process.phases: Phase 0: extract {{3}} representative files, show me those rows only → GATE (sample). Phase 1: batch. Phase 2: QA — re-open {{5}} random files, verify their rows side-by-side against the originals.

custom.task.statement: Compare {{options}} for {{the decision}}. Study each independently first (key facts, each with link + date), then head-to-head on {{criteria}}, then a recommendation with the two decisive factors and what would change your mind.
custom.format.output_type: Deliver in three layers: findings summary → comparison matrix (criteria × options) → slide outline (titles state findings with numbers).

custom.task.statement:
Build a scored comparison workbook: rows = {{options}}, columns = {{criteria, with weights}}.
Tabs: README (criteria definitions, weights, sources, as-of date) · Scores (raw + weighted — formulas, not pasted values) · Result (ranking + a sensitivity note: what change would flip #1?).

custom.a_mission.goal: Update {{workbook / deck}} for {{new period}} keeping its existing structure exactly — same tabs/slides, same definitions and names, new data only.
custom.a_inputs.register:
S1 — the current version at {{path}} (structure + prior numbers = the contract)
S2 — new-period data at {{path}}
custom.a_checks.anchor: the prior version's published totals — every carried-over figure must match it exactly
custom.a_outputs.deliverables:
1. A NEW file with today's _MMDDYY suffix — never overwrite the previous version.
2. A delta note: every headline metric vs. last period, one line each.
